_meta.indication: Treatment of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) in adult patients who remain symptomatic despite H1 antihistamine treatment; not indicated for other forms of urticaria

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 2:1 randomization to remibrutinib 25 mg or placebo twice daily for 24-week controlled period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with CSU inadequately controlled despite H1 antihistamines, with UAS7 ≥ 16, ISS7 ≥ 6, and HSS7 ≥ 6
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Coprimary: absolute change from baseline in ISS7 and HSS7 at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: ISS7 treatment difference -2.63 (95% CI -3.70, -1.56; p<0.001); HSS7 difference -3.61 (95% CI -4.85, -2.36; p<0.001) at Week 12

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; identical to REMIX-1
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with CSU inadequately controlled despite H1 antihistamines, with UAS7 ≥ 16, ISS7 ≥ 6, and HSS7 ≥ 6
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Coprimary: absolute change from baseline in ISS7 and HSS7 at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: ISS7 treatment difference -3.23 (95% CI -4.29, -2.16; p<0.001); HSS7 difference -4.47 (95% CI -5.71, -3.23; p<0.001) at Week 12

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 3%): nasopharyngitis (11% vs 9% placebo), bleeding (9% vs 2%), headache (7% vs 6%), nausea (3% vs 2%), abdominal pain (3% vs 2%). Bleeding is an identified risk (Warning and Precaution)
target_moa: Oral small molecule kinase inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK); inhibits mast cell and basophil degranulation mediated by pathogenic IgE or IgG directed against FcεR1 or IgE

rems.type: No REMS is required; potential risks addressed through labeling and pharmacovigilance

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise unexpected safety/efficacy or controversial issues

summary.text: NDA 218436 for remibrutinib (RHAPSIDO), an oral BTK inhibitor, was reviewed on a priority review timeline because the Applicant redeemed a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher; it did not have breakthrough therapy designation or otherwise meet priority review criteria, was not taken to an advisory committee, and was approved based on two replicate phase 3 trials.

citations.quote: The Applicant, Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation, submitted NDA 218436 for remibrutinib (tradename: RHAPSIDO), an oral inhibitor of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK), for "the treatment of chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) in adult patients who remain symptomatic despite H1-antihistamine treatment" at a proposed dosage of 25 mg orally twice daily. Because the Applicant redeemed a priority review
Trials A2301 and A2302 were replicate phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials that enrolled 925 adults to evaluate remibrutinib 25 mg orally twice daily over 52 weeks.

Although remibrutinib does not have breakthrough therapy designation for this indication nor meet criteria for a priority review, the Applicant submitted the NDA using the Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher (NDA 217759); therefore, this application was granted a priority review.

This application was not taken to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from discussion by an advisory committee.

requirement.text: 4896-1 Conduct a 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study in pediatric patients aged 12 to less than 18 years with chronic spontaneous urticaria who remain symptomatic despite H1-antihistamine treatment to assess the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic responses to remibrutinib.

citations.quote: 4896-1 Conduct a 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study in pediatric patients aged 12 to less than 18 years with chronic spontaneous urticaria who remain symptomatic despite H1-antihistamine treatment to assess the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetic responses to remibrutinib.

requirement.text: 4896-2 Conduct a 24-week, open-label, pharmacokinetic study in pediatric patients aged 6 to less than 12 years with chronic spontaneous urticaria who remain symptomatic despite H1-antihistamine treatment.

requirement.text: 4896-3 Conduct an additional oral (gavage) juvenile toxicity study in the rat. The age of rats at study start should be equivalent to pediatric patients approximately 6 years old. The study should include ophthalmic examinations performed pre-study, at the end of the dosing period, and at the end of the recovery period. Potential neurobehavioral effects should also be evaluated in animals at the end of the dosing and recovery periods.

requirement.text: 4896-4 Collect data from a prospective pregnancy exposure registry, preferably a disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry, using a cohort analysis that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to remibrutinib during pregnancy with an appropriate comparator population(s).

citations.quote: 4896-4 Collect data from a prospective pregnancy exposure registry, preferably a disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry, using a cohort analysis that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to remibrutinib during pregnancy with an appropriate comparator population(s). Collect data outside the U.S. to reach the target sample size, if feasible. The registry will identify and record major and minor congenital malformations, pregnancy complications, spontaneous abortion, stillbirths, neonatal deaths, pregnancy terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births, and any other adverse outcomes, including postnatal growth and development. These outcomes should be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4896-5 Conduct a retrospective pregnancy cohort study using claims or electronic health record data with medical chart validation that is adequately powered to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, preterm births, and small-for-gestational-age births in women exposed to remibrutinib during pregnancy compared to appropriate comparator population(s).

requirement.text: 4896-6 Perform a milk-only lactation study in lactating women who have received remibrutinib to measure concentrations of remibrutinib in breast milk using a validated assay. Assess the effects on the breastfed infant, if available, based on study population.
